column3: note
column5: note

column3: Faithful to Mark 4:1, 35-41; the closing names who the storm obeyed and promises no calm to the listener.
column5: Plain, warm, no stock phrases; the hospital and bills line is ordinary life, not a stereotype.

column3: Faithful to Exodus 14; the Egyptians' end is told plainly without gloating; credit stays with the LORD.
column5: Families and elders shown with dignity; no slavery imagery beyond what the text says.

column3: Faithful to Daniel 6:1-23; no promise that the listener's lions will be shut; prayer habit is the point.
column5: Clear and calm; the king is shown as torn, not mocked.

column3: Faithful to Jonah 1-2 and 3:1-3; God's charge paraphrased in the third person, never as God speaking.
column5: Neutral voice; the sailors are treated with respect.

column3: Faithful to 1 Samuel 17; the close says plainly the story does not promise every fight ends this way.
column5: No violence beyond the text; plain and vivid.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 37 with 39:2 named as later; does not soften the brothers' sin.
column5: The sale of a free person is told as the wrong it was; no servitude framing of Joseph's worth.

column3: Faithful to Luke 15:11-32 after one fix; ends on the father going to both sons, no claim about the listener's standing.
column5: Plain and kind; the elder son is not made a villain.
column6: Pastor pass: removed an outside claim about what older men did in that culture; replaced with the verse's own action.

column3: Faithful to Ruth 1; lets Naomi's lament stand; the harvest line stays inside the text.
column5: Orpah is not blamed; Ruth's loyalty is told with dignity.

column3: Faithful to Daniel 3; 'but if not' carried without promising rescue; no speculation on who the fourth was.
column5: Steady and plain; the king is not caricatured.

column3: Faithful to Mark 5:22-34 and 5:42; the healing stays hers in the text, no healing promise to the listener.
column5: The woman is seen and named daughter; nothing pitying or exploitative about her illness.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 6-9; the rainbow is told as God's covenant, not a promise about the listener's storms.
column5: Plain and gentle; the loss in the flood is stated without spectacle.
column6: Pastor pass: cut an invented detail (years of building far from any sea); Genesis gives neither.

column3: Faithful to Esther 2-5; the harem context is left out rather than retold; 'if I perish' kept without promising safety to the listener.
column5: Esther shown as brave and wise, an orphan raised by family; no exoticising of the court.

column3: Faithful to Job 1-2 and 42; no reason for suffering invented; the satan scenes are left out, not reinterpreted; restoration not presented as a formula.
column5: Grief told plainly; the friends' seven days of silence honoured.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 1:1-2:3; 'care of the earth' summarises dominion without taking a side on how the days are read.
column5: Calm and plain; 'every person carries that image' said without any race claim.

column3: Faithful to John 4; her marriages stated without moralising, as Jesus does; Jesus's identity stated as the text states it.
column5: She is not made a sinner-stereotype; she becomes the town's witness.
column6: Pastor pass: removed an outside claim about when women drew water and an overstated 'first witness in John'; replaced with the sixth hour and verse 39.

column3: Faithful to Matthew 14:22-33; closing describes what the disciples saw, no promise that the listener will be caught from every fall.
column5: Peter's doubt handled kindly; plain voice.
column6: Pastor pass: replaced a general promise ('his hand reaches the one who cries out') with what the text shows.

column3: Faithful to Exodus 3:1-14 with 2:15 as background; God's words only in KJV blocks, read by the narrator.
column5: Plain and reverent.
column6: Pastor pass: removed a borrowed line (Hebrews 13:8) added to the meaning of I AM.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 41-50 as cited; forgiveness shown without excusing the brothers' sin.
column5: Tender without melodrama; the slave years named honestly, not romanticised.

column3: Faithful to Luke 10:38-42; Martha's serving is not condemned; no doctrine of women's roles added.
column5: Both sisters treated with dignity; Martha is not the villain.
column6: Pastor pass: removed an outside claim about where students sat and an invented 'more guests than planned'.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kings 17:1-16; the close says plainly it does not promise every empty cupboard will be filled; no seed-faith reading.
column5: The widow is poor but never pitiable or comic; a foreign woman honoured.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 2:7-3:23; no doctrine of the fall added; God's questions read as the text gives them; ends on God clothing them.
column5: Neither the man nor the woman is made the villain; the blame-passing is named for both.

column3: Faithful to 1 Samuel 1; states plainly the story does not promise a child to everyone who prays; peace before the answer is the point.
column5: Hannah's grief and Peninnah's taunting told without cruelty; childlessness handled with care.

column3: Faithful to Luke 19:1-10; grace before change; no prosperity reading of his giving.
column5: His height and his town's contempt told without mockery.
column6: Pastor pass: removed outside claims about Roman tax practice; kept to what Jericho said in verse 7.

column3: Faithful to Mark 2:1-12; forgiveness and healing both kept, no promise of healing to the listener.
column5: Disability shown with dignity; the man is not a prop, his friends are honoured.
column6: Pastor pass: cut an invented 'long way' and a flat-roof claim; the text says they uncovered the roof.

column3: Faithful to Luke 2:1-20; angels' words only in KJV blocks; no extra-biblical detail (no innkeeper, no animals named).
column5: Working people honoured as the first to hear; plain and warm.

column3: Faithful to Judges 4:1-16 and 5:1-3; Jael's act is left out (not retold), the 'hand of a woman' line kept; Barak's request given two readings, no side taken.
column5: A woman judge and prophet shown with full authority and dignity.

column3: Faithful to 2 Kings 4:1-7; says outright it is not a promise that giving or pouring makes anyone rich; no seed-faith reading.
column5: The widow is resourceful, not pitiable; the neighbours' jars honoured.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 12:1-8 and 15:1-6; faith counted as righteousness stated as the text states it; no outcome promise.
column5: An old man starting over told with dignity.

column3: Faithful to Luke 10:25-37; the priest and Levite are not made a lesson against clergy beyond the text.
column5: Enmity between Jews and Samaritans told without disparaging either people.

column3: Faithful to Exodus 1:8-10, 1:22 and 2:1-10; the decree stated, not dwelt on.
column5: Three women honoured: mother, sister and princess; the Egyptian princess is not villainised.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 18:1-4 and 20:35-42; Saul's turn against David is the chapters' own context (19-20), told briefly; the covenant is put in the LORD's keeping as v42 says, no promise to the listener.
column5: Plain and warm; two men weeping is shown with dignity and without comment on anything the text does not say.
column6: Free draft paraphrased each verse right before it; cut the repeats, fixed the arrow-signal speech cuts, added why David hid.

column3: Faithful to John 11:17-44; Jesus's words stay in scripture blocks; removed the draft's invented detail (grave clothes falling away) and a near-"speak life" phrase.
column5: Grief shown as heavy and real, not hurried; plain voice.
column6: Free draft invented the ending detail; rewritten close to the text.

column3: Faithful to Judges 6:11-16 and 7:2-8; the numbers match the text; the point is v2's (no one boasts, the LORD saves).
column5: Plain; Gideon's honest question is respected, not mocked.
column6: Light edit: cut repeats, LORD as in the text.

column3: Faithful to Mark 5:21-24, 35-43; mentions the healing on the way (5:25-34) in one line without retelling it; no promise that the listener's child will be raised.
column5: A father's fear told plainly; the mourners are not caricatured.
column6: Free draft paraphrased most verses before quoting them; trimmed.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 32:6-12 and 33:1-11; the stolen blessing is Genesis 27, named as context; the face-of-God line is v10's own.
column5: Brothers reconciled with dignity; no blame beyond the text.
column6: Moderate edit: context added, repeats cut, a typed-scripture run reworded.

column3: Faithful to John 6:1-14; the boy's lunch and the twelve baskets as given; no promise of provision to the listener.
column5: Plain, warm; barley bread named as ordinary people's food without a poverty stereotype.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 3:1-10; God's words stay with the narrator in scripture blocks; Hannah named as 1 Sam 1 gives.
column5: A child's obedience shown gently; plain voice.
column6: Free draft (second route) broke the source format and invented temple details; rewritten by Claude.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kings 3:16-28 (and 3:9 for the request); the speech of the one woman and the true mother kept separate, as the text does not say they are the same; the women's trade (v16) is left in the stored verse, not dwelt on.
column5: Both women shown as people, not types; the king's wisdom credited to God as v28.
column6: Moderate edit: speech cuts fixed, the real mother's plea (v26) added as scripture.

column3: Faithful to Mark 10:46-52; Jesus's question and answer stay with the narrator; the name as spelled in the stored KJV.
column5: A blind beggar shown with agency and dignity; the crowd's change is told without scorn.
column6: Moderate edit: verse split fixed, repeats cut.

column3: Faithful to Exodus 19:16-20 and 20:1-17, the commandments themselves as scripture blocks, never paraphrased in God's voice; the sabbath is the text's own word with no position on which day; the rescue comes before the law, as 20:2 says.
column5: Plain and reverent; no moralising beyond the text.
column6: Free draft retold each commandment in narration before quoting it; rewritten around the verses.

column3: Faithful to Matt 25:14-29; stops before v30 (outer darkness) so the plain shelf does not threaten; the talent explained as money held in trust, and the close says outright it is not a story about getting rich (no prosperity reading); v29 left with the narrator, as the text does not mark the speaker.
column5: Plain and warm; the third servant shown as afraid, not lazy-mocked; no class or money stereotypes.

column3: Faithful to Josh 2:1-21 (verses 7, 10, 16-17, 19-20 summarised in narration, nothing added); her trade is left in the stored verse and named once, gently; her later place in Israel is Josh 6:25 and her faith Heb 11:31, stated without a reference in the text.
column5: Rahab shown with agency, courage and faith, never as a joke or a type; her care for her family kept.

column3: Faithful to Josh 6:1-20; God's commands read by the narrator as scripture; ends at v20, the slaughter of v21 not told; the close is about God keeping his word to Israel, with no promise that a listener's own walls will fall.
column5: Plain; Rahab remembered by name; no triumphalism over the people of Jericho.

column3: Faithful to John 3:1-17; Jesus's words only as scripture; water and Spirit left uninterpreted (no position on baptism); the bronze serpent is Num 21; Nicodemus later is John 7:50 and 19:39; no telling the listener she is saved or lost.
column5: A seeker shown with dignity; questions honoured, not scolded.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 25:14-35 (v22 and v34's coarse phrase left out by choosing verses, not by changing them); the set-up (vv 2-13) told plainly from the text; credit to God as David gives it in v32.
column5: Abigail shown as wise and brave, a woman whose word turns an army; Nabal named a fool only as the text and his wife do.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kings 19:1-15 (the 7,000 is v18); Elijah's wish to die told honestly and gently; God's care is rest, food and a quiet word; the close points a weary listener to a person who loves her, with no promise of an outcome. A deacon board would read it aloud.
column5: Tender, not preachy; despair is not shamed.

column3: Faithful to Mark 10:17-27; 'young' and 'ruler' attributed to the other gospels (Matt 19:20, Luke 18:18); no rule that all must sell everything and no claim that wealth damns; the point is v27, with God.
column5: Plain; the rich man shown as sincere and sad, not mocked.

column3: Faithful to Gen 24:10-27 (v16's description skipped, nothing changed); the servant's prayer and thanks kept as scripture; nothing invented about Rebekah beyond her kindness in the text.
column5: Rebekah's kindness and work shown with dignity; no romance framing.

column3: Faithful to Judges 16:4-30 (vv 7-14 summarised; 'green withs' told as fresh bowstrings); tagged violence strong, adult shelf, the death count left in the stored verse; his mixed motive (v28) not praised; Heb 11:32 cited in words, not reference.
column5: Delilah shown as bought, not as a seductress caricature; no sexual detail; Samson's failures told plainly.

column3: Faithful to Matt 2:1-12; stops before v16 (the children of Bethlehem); the number and status of the wise men not invented ('perhaps'); the gifts named as the text names them.
column5: Strangers from the east honoured; plain and reverent.

column3: Faithful to John 2:1-11; 'woman' explained as respectful, Mary's word to the servants kept as scripture; nothing said for or against drinking; the jar size is the text's firkins in plain measure.
column5: Mary shown as wise and trusted; the servants as the ones who saw; warm and plain.

column3: Faithful to Num 22:21-35; the angel of the LORD read by the narrator only; the set-up (22:1-20) and the blessings (Num 23-24) told plainly without invented speech; humour is the text's own.
column5: The donkey is the hero and the joke is on the proud man, not on any people; 'donkey' in narration, the KJV word left in the verses.

column3: Faithful to Luke 15:1-7; the coin and the son named as the chapter's other two stories; no claim on who is lost tonight, only the shepherd's search.
column5: Tax collectors and sinners shown as welcomed, not mocked; the grumblers answered, not scorned.

column3: Faithful to Gen 29:9-30; tagged sexual implied (v23 left out of the verses, the swap told in one plain sentence); Leah seen by God is v31, Judah to David to Jesus is the genealogy (Ruth 4, Matt 1), stated without references; 'tender eyed' left uncertain as it is.
column5: Leah treated with tenderness, never as a joke about looks; the hurt of all three told honestly; no romance gloss on Laban's trick.

column3: Faithful to Luke 16:19-31; the narration says it is not a map of the afterlife and never tells the listener she is bound anywhere; the point is v29 and v31, hearing now; 'Lazarus means God helps' is the name's usual sense.
column5: The poor man has the name and the dignity; no poverty-only framing beyond the text; the rich man's sin is neglect, not wealth itself.

column3: Faithful to John 13:1-17; no position on foot washing as a church practice (some churches keep it, most do not); Judas's feet washed is in the text (v11-12).
column5: Service shown as love, not servitude; Peter's swing told with warmth.

column3: Faithful to Acts 9:1-19; the Lord's words read by the narrator; v18's baptism left in the stored verse without comment; Saul to Paul is Acts 13:9.
column5: Ananias, the ordinary believer, is the quiet hero; 'brother' as the turn; no shaming of Saul's people.

column3: Faithful to Luke 23:33-47; crucifixion tagged violence mild and kept off the page (no wound detail); no blame of 'the Jews' for the death; 'today' given as the text gives it, no doctrine of what paradise is; ends in stillness, pointing on to the resurrection.
column5: Reverent; the dying thief shown with dignity; a deacon board would read it on Good Friday.

column3: Faithful to John 20:1-18; the Sabbath named only as the day between (no position on which day to keep); 'the other disciple' left unnamed as the text leaves him; Mary as first witness is the text.
column5: Mary Magdalene shown as faithful and the first sent, never with the later legends about her past.

column3: Faithful to Luke 24:13-35; the breaking of bread told as the text tells it, with no position on communion; Jesus's teaching summarised from v26-27 without new words put in his mouth.
column5: Grief and lost hope honoured; plain and hopeful; ends on the story's truth.
